The theorems used are called KAM for conviencences based on the three founders of many of the theorems. KAM Torii

Essentially, KAM is the study of how nearly integratable Hamiltonians remain similar to their integratable counterparts. Resonance refers to ones that remain.

Ergodic Theorem

The Ergodic theorem states that the long time average of a function over phase space is equal to the ensemble average.(essentially the average of one function is the same as the average over the collection of possible states of a system)

This theorem is valid for dynamics \(\theta ' = \theta \alpha(r)\), provided \(\alpha\) is irrational.

We may compute the difference between \(f_0\) from the theorem would be

\[\delta f(\theta) = \sum_{k=1}^\infty \left[a_k e^{ik\theta} + a^{*}_ke^{-ik\theta} \right]\]

assuming that \(\abs{a_k} < \frac{a_1}{k^2}\) to eliminate discontinuous functions. Summing this we can get that the sum diverges wher \(k \alpha = 2 \pi m\). The sum will converge provided that \[\abs{\frac{\alpha}{2 \pi} - \frac{m}{n} > \frac{\epsilon}{n^3}}\]

not here that m and n are integers, particular resonance between the frequencies \(\alpha = (m/n)2 \pi\)
